name: Tunisian Arabic Corpus (tunisiya.org)
description: Raw reference corpus with a searchable concordance interface. Karen McNeil and Miled Faiza.

name: CTAB — Corpus of Tunisian Arabizi
description: Raw, unannotated Arabizi (Latin-script) corpus. Amara et al., 2021. Facebook public-page messages kept as-is, grouped by page/period. Companion to tunisiya.org.

name: tunisian-derja-unified-raw-corpus
description: Aggregated raw corpus, ~802,659 text examples (~860k rows). Merges social media, conversational transcripts, chatbot dialogues, and other public Derja datasets; preserves French/English code-switching. Hamza Bouajila, 2025. Seed corpus for the ESPRIT-Derja model.

name: linagora/Tunisian_Derja_Dataset
description: Large aggregated Derja LM corpus, ~2.23M rows / 332 MB, cc-by-sa-4.0. Wajdi Ghezaiel and Jean-Pierre Lorré (LINAGORA), 2025. Aggregates 14 sub-corpora (khaled123 Derja-English, TSAC, TunBERT, TunSwitch, TuDiCoI, QADI-TN, MADAR-TN, TA-Segmentation, Tweet_TN, and more). Used to continual-pretrain the Labess LLM.

name: linagora/fineweb2_Tunisian_Arabic
description: The Tunisian (`aeb`) portion of FineWeb2, ~265k rows. LINAGORA, June 2025. ODC-By v1.0.

name: Tunisian_reddit
description: Raw social-media corpus scraped from r/Tunisia (posts + comments, 2009–2022, two CSVs; scraper scripts included). Uncurated; HF size category 100K–1M rows, ~3.4 GB on disk; no exact row count published (the HF viewer cannot convert it). MIT, uploaded Dec 2023.

name: AzizBelaweid/Tunisian_Language_Dataset
description: **269,773** rows, single `text` column, ~618 MB. Licence tag CC-BY-4.0, but the card body says CC BY-SA 4.0 ("the most restrictive license terms of its components") — the two disagree; assume BY-SA. Mohamed Aziz Belaweid, 2024. Publishes its own `create_data.py` and `preprocess.py`, so the build is reproducible — unusual and welcome for a community dump.

name: Syrinesmati/tunisian-dialect-corpus
description: **1,180,174** rows, `text` + `source`, ~208 MB parquet. Apache-2.0, 2026.

name: Nehdi/TuniziBigBench
description: Despite the name, a raw corpus, not an evaluation benchmark: a single TSV of Tunizi (Arabizi) text scraped from 14,000+ Tunisian YouTube videos, HF size category 1M–10M rows, tagged text-classification. Nov 2024; licence creativeml-openrail-m. **[open]** (HuggingFace).

name: TSAC — Tunisian Sentiment Analysis Corpus
description: Binary sentiment (positive/negative). Medhaffar, Bougares, Estève, Hadrich-Belguith, 2017.

name: TUNIZI — Tunisian Arabizi Sentiment Dataset (v1)
description: Sentiment on Latin-script (Arabizi) Tunisian. Fourati, Messaoudi, Haddad (iCompass), 2020. The linked repo and its HF mirror hold **3,000** YouTube comments (1,500 positive / 1,500 negative); the iCompass-ai repo's `TUNIZI_V1.txt` is described there as 9,210 sentences — the two "v1" releases differ in size.

name: TUNIZI v2 — Large Tunisian Arabizi Dataset
description: Extended Arabizi sentiment set, ~100k comments (movies, politics, sport…) labeled positive/negative/neutral. iCompass, 2021.

name: arbml/Tunisian_Dialect_Corpus
description: Polarity classification (negative/positive), 49,889 rows, Arabic + Arabizi. Aggregated Tunisian tweets/comments.

name: hedhoud12/TunisianSentimentAnalysis
description: Sentiment corpus, ~23,786 rows. Hedi Naouara (LINAGORA), Oct 2024.

name: T-HSAB — Tunisian Hate Speech and Abusive Dataset
description: Three classes: normal / abusive / hate. Haddad, Mulki, Oueslati, 2019 (Springer ICALP proceedings, CCIS 1108, pp. 251–263). 6,024 comments per the repo README (the TEET! paper cites 6,039).

name: TEET! — Tunisian Dataset for Toxic Speech Detection
description: Toxic-speech corpus, ~10,000 comments. Gharbi, Haddad, Kchaou, Arfaoui, 2021. Paper is open; a public data repo was not confirmed.

name: HateTune — Tunisian Dialect Hate Speech Detection Dataset
description: Hate speech in Arabic-script Tunisian: 12k+ comments, Hate/Neutral. Kharrat, Mohamed, Mtimet, Benamor, Fourati (MedTech); ICALP 2024 proceedings, published Feb 2025 (CCIS 2339, pp. 63–73). The abstract calls it "the largest publicly available dataset" for the task; the footnoted data link could not be resolved when checked (4 Sept 2026).

name: TDMulti — Tunisian Dialect–MSA Multitask Corpus
description: First multitask Tunisian corpus manually aligned with MSA: 3,100 social-media comments, 12,400 labels across **hate speech, sentiment polarity, sarcasm, and topic**, with a context-aware cross-attention BERT model. Torjmen, Haddar, LREC 2026 (pp. 3240–3249).

name: MADAR Corpus and Lexicon
description: Multi-dialect parallel corpus + city/country dialect ID (26-way). Bouamor et al., LREC 2018. Includes **Tunis** (Corpus-26/Corpus-6) and **Sfax** in the lexicon.

name: NADI — Nuanced Arabic Dialect Identification
description: Country/province-level dialect ID from tweets, annual 2020–2024. Tunisia is one of ~21 covered countries.

name: IADD — Integrated Arabic Dialect Identification Dataset
description: Aggregated dialect-ID dataset merging DART, SHAMI, PADIC, AOC, and **TSAC** — so it embeds a Tunisian subset. Jihad Zahir (single author), Data in Brief 40, 2022 (online Dec 2021). 136,317 texts from 9 countries, Tunisia included.

name: QADI — QCRI Arabic Dialect Identification
description: Country-level dialect-ID tweets across 18 countries; the Tunisian subset is ~8,879 items (as folded into the LinTO Derja aggregate). QCRI.

name: ArapTweet
description: Large multi-dialect Arabic Twitter corpus for gender, age, and language-variety identification, covering 11 Arab regions including Tunisia. Zaghouani and Charfi, LREC 2018.

name: Multi-Dialect, Multi-Genre Corpus of Informal Written Arabic (LREC 2014)
description: Cotterell and Callison-Burch. Informal Arabic across five dialect groups including **Maghrebi** (Tunisian-relevant). Paper: LREC 2014, #641 (PDF). **[on request]**.

name: Arabic Dialect Identification shared-task data (LREC 2018)
description: Dialect-ID train/test data under `ArabicSharedTask/`. ⚠️ The repo carries no README or paper reference and its own description reads "test files not a real project" — recorded, not vouched for.

name: PADIC — Parallel Arabic Dialect Corpus
description: Cross-listed. Also usable for dialect ID; one of six dialects is Tunisian. Full details under Machine translation and parallel corpora. **[open]**.

name: Sub-dialect identification (within Tunisian)
description: Text and Speech-based Tunisian Arabic Sub-Dialects Identification (LREC 2020) — Ben Abdallah, Kchaou, Bougares. Distinguishes Tunis / Sfax / Sousse / Tataouine. A released benchmark rather than an organized competition. **[open]** (paper).

name: TArC — Tunisian Arabish Corpus
description: Multi-layer annotated Arabizi corpus. Gugliotta and Dinarelli; first release 2020, complete release 2022.

name: TTB — Tunisian Treebank + parser
description: Constituency/syntactic treebank and a trained Stanford-parser model. Mekki, Zribi, Ellouze, Belguith, 2020.

name: TADT — Tunisian Arabic Dependency Treebank (Universal Dependencies)
description: The first UD treebank for Tunisian (`aeb`). Amal Aissaoui (CUNY), 2026. 100 sentences / 1,466 tokens of Arabizi social-media text (sampled from CTAB), with UPOS, morphological features, lemmas, and dependency relations. Built by cross-dialect transfer from the Algerian NArabizi treebank + manual correction.

name: TA-Segmentation Corpus
description: Sentence-boundary / segmentation annotation with CODA-TA normalization. Mekki et al., 2021. 260,364 words / 33,581 sentences, expert-validated.

name: TArC POS layer
description: See TArC (repo): POS (Penn Arabic Treebank style) is applied to the *arabizi* tokens — 31,510 of the corpus's 43,327 tokens (the rest are tagged foreign/emotag). **[open]**.

name: POS-tagging of Tunisian Dialect Using Standard Arabic Resources (WANLP 2015)
description: Hamdi, Nasr, Habash, Gala. Maps Tunisian to an MSA lattice and tags with an MSA tagger (~89% accuracy). Method paper; no standalone gold TD POS corpus released. **[open]** (paper).

name: Fine-Grained POS Tagging of Spoken Tunisian Dialect (Springer NLDB 2014)
description: Boujelbane, Mallek, Ellouze, Hadrich-Belguith. Builds a TD training corpus by converting an MSA corpus via a bilingual lexicon (~78.5% accuracy).

name: Intelligent Tunisian Arabic Morphological Analyzer — evaluation corpus
description: 1,000 Tunisian words used to evaluate the Karmani analyzer. Karmani, Soussou, Alimi, AICCSA 2016.

name: Tunisian-Arabic-Lexical-Dictionary
description: XML lexicon of the main Tunisian clitics (repo description: "Main TA clitics"). Same author as the analyzer above.

name: Al-Khalil-TUN — Morphological Analysis of Tunisian Dialect (IJCNLP 2013)
description: Zribi, Ellouze Khemakhem, Hadrich Belguith. Adapts the MSA Al-Khalil analyzer with a Tunisian lexicon of 6,030 roots and 6,092 patterns built from the 27,144-word STAC corpus. No public download of the analyzer or lexicon was found.

name: Morphological Disambiguation of Tunisian Dialect (J. King Saud Univ., 2017)
description: Zribi, Ellouze, Hadrich-Belguith, Blache. ML disambiguation over the analyzer output. Journal of King Saud University – Computer and Information Sciences 29(2), pp. 147–155 (CC BY-NC-ND). **[open]** (article; the ResearchGate link is a bot-walled mirror — use DOI 10.1016/j.jksuci.2017.01.004).

name: Barcha
description: Open multi-purpose Tunisian resource (MIT). wa3dbk. Its `named_entities/` folder is a set of curated Tunisian entity gazetteers: people (academics/scientists, artists, footballers, media figures, poets, politicians, trade unionists, writers), institutions/associations/companies, government institutions, cities, universities (public and private), ISETs, political parties, and unions. Also ships a `texts/` raw-text folder and a `translation/` folder — the README still lists Tunisian↔English/MSA parallel sets as a TODO, so treat that folder as work in progress.

name: TUNER — NER of Tunisian Arabic with Bi-LSTM-CRF (2023/2024)
description: Mekki, Zribi, Ellouze, Belguith. Hybrid Bi-LSTM-CRF + rules, F-measure 91.43% (abstract); online 2023, IJAIT 33(2) 2024. No public release of the annotated NER corpus was found.

name: Recognition and Translation of Tunisian Dialect Named Entities into MSA (2021)
description: Torjmen and Haddar. No public dataset found.

name: PADIC — Parallel Arabic Dialect Corpus
description: Parallel dialect corpus. Meftouh, Harrat, Abbas, Smaïli (SMarT/LORIA); Tunisian portion by Salma Jamoussi. 2015, extended 2017–2018.

name: MADAR Parallel Corpus
description: Corpus-26: 2,000 BTEC sentences translated into 25 city dialects + MSA (includes **Tunis** and **Sfax**). Corpus-6: 12,000 sentences in 5 cities + MSA (includes **Tunis**). Bouamor et al., LREC 2018.

name: MDC — Multidialectal Parallel Corpus of Arabic
description: 2,000 sentences in MSA, Egyptian, **Tunisian**, Jordanian, Palestinian, Syrian + English. Bouamor, Habash, Oflazer, LREC 2014.

name: Parallel resources for Tunisian Arabic Dialect Translation (WANLP 2020)
description: Kchaou, Boujelbane, Hadrich-Belguith. Tunisian (social media) ↔ MSA with data augmentation; BLEU up to 15.03.

name: Rule-based / SMT Tunisian→MSA
description: Rule-Based MT from Tunisian to MSA (Procedia 2020) — Sghaier and Zrigui. **[open]**.

name: tunisian-darija-english (Dhia Azizi)
description: 553 Tunisian Arabizi↔English pairs across 53 cultural categories (louage culture, mawsem el zitoun, bac exam culture, el 3aza w mawt…). Every pair provenance-tagged in a `source` column: 500 self-written by the author (native speaker), 53 field-collected from family and community speakers with documented consent; nothing synthetic. Dhia Azizi, 2026; collection ongoing.

name: Community HuggingFace parallel sets
description: tunis-ai/tunisian-msa-parallel-corpus — 1,000 Derja↔MSA pairs (synthetic pipeline, CC-BY-4.0). Tunisia.AI, 2025. **[open]**. Companion tunis-ai/tunisian-msa-parallel-corpus-evaluated — the same **1,000 rows** quality-graded (CC-BY-4.0, tagged `aeb`) with `semantic_similarity`, `fluency_score` and `composite_score` per pair alongside raw and cleaned MSA translations. It is the scored view of the corpus, not additional data; the per-pair scores make it the more useful of the two for building an evaluation split.

name: Speech translation corpora with Tunisian↔English/French text
description: Pointer entry. **TuniFra** (Tunisian→French, 15 h), **TEDxTN** (Tunisian→English, ~25 h) and the **IWSLT 2022/2023 Tunisian–English** LDC corpus are three-way (audio + transcript + translation) and are listed in SPEECH.md; their transcript/translation layers are also Tunisian–French / Tunisian–English bitext. TuniFra and TEDxTN are **[open]** (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0); the LDC corpus is **[paywalled]**.

name: Romanized Arabic Across Dialects (five-dialect Arabizi study)
description: The largest human-centered cross-dialect study of Arabizi perception and usage to date, covering Algerian, Egyptian, Lebanese, Moroccan, and **Tunisian** Arabic. Announces two resources: character-level Arabic↔Arabizi alignments from survey-participant transliterations, and a manually curated parallel corpus of Arabic-script sentences with multiple Arabizi transliterations per dialect. Keleg, Ben Abdallah, Yassine, Helwe, Guellil, Ousidhoum, 2026.

name: TArC
description: Annotated Arabizi corpus and the neural tool that transliterates Arabizi→CODA Arabic script and does tokenization/POS. Gugliotta, Dinarelli, Kraif. Code on GitLab. **[open]**.

name: Masmoudi et al. — Arabizi→Arabic-script transliteration for Tunisian
description: Transliteration of Arabizi into Arabic Script for Tunisian Dialect (ACM TALLIP 2019) — rule-based + CRF; the abstract reports a character error rate of 10.47%. **[paywalled]**.

name: Younes et al. — bi-script Tunisian resources
description: Romanized Tunisian Dialect Transliteration using Sequence Labelling (J. King Saud Univ. 2020). **[open]** (paper).

name: A Conventional Orthography for Tunisian Arabic (CODA-TUN)
description: The canonical Tunisian CODA spec (Arabic-script conventional orthography). Zribi, Boujelbane, Masmoudi, Ellouze, Belguith, Habash, LREC 2014. PDF. **[open]**.

name: CODA* — Unified Guidelines and Resources for Arabic Dialect Orthography
description: Cross-dialect orthography framework covering 28 city dialects, Tunis included. Habash et al., LREC 2018. PDF. **[open]**.

name: A Conventional Orthography for Maghrebi Arabic (LREC 2016)
description: Turki, Adel, Daouda, Regragui. Extends CODA across Maghrebi Arabic (Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco, Libya, Mauritania). Not in the ACL Anthology; copies on ResearchGate and Academia. **[open]** (paper).

name: NOTA — Normalized Orthography for Tunisian Arabic (Springer 2025)
description: Turki, Ellouze, Ben Ammar, Hadj Taieb, Adel, Ben Aouicha, Farri, Bennour; LPKM 2024 (Sfax), Springer LNNS, published Mar 2025. **[paywalled]** (Springer).

name: aebWordNet — Lexicon
description: Tunisian (`aeb`) WordNet lexicon (XML). Karmani, Soussou, Alimi (Research Groups on Intelligent Machines, Univ. of Sfax), ACLing 2015. **[open]** (GitHub; ACLing 2015 paper paywalled).

name: TunDiaWN — Tunisian dialect WordNet (WANLP 2014)
description: Bouchlaghem, Elkhlifi, Faiz (EMNLP 2014 Arabic NLP workshop, Doha). Corpus-based wordnet reusing English + Arabic wordnets. Database not found for download.

name: Peace Corps English–Tunisian Arabic Dictionary
description: 1977 two-way English↔Tunisian dictionary with phonetic symbols and grammar notes. Companion Peace Corps Tunisian Arabic course. **[open]** (Internet Archive).

name: Derja.Ninja
description: Community Tunisian↔English dictionary, ~17,000 entries with example sentences and audio. Scraper: ArmelVidali/derja_ninja_scraper. **[open]** (web).

name: Webonary "Tunsi" dictionary
description: Online Tunisian (Latin-script)–German dictionary, 276 entries when checked (Sept 2026); Ramzi Hachani, 2025. **[open]** (web).

name: Wiktionary — Tunisian Arabic
description: Collaborative lexicon plus a Swadesh list. **[open]**.

name: Bilingual lexicons from the literature (Tunisian↔MSA)
description: Boujelbane et al., Building bilingual lexicon to create Dialect Tunisian corpora (HyTra workshop, ACL 2013). **[paper only]**.

name: Tunisian Proverbs with Image Associations
description: **999** Tunisian proverbs, each with an Arabic explanation, a `context` field, two English rendering layers (`caption` word-for-word and `dynamic` for the functional equivalent), a `caption_formal` variant, the generation `prompt`, **up to four AI-generated images**, and a `clip_scores` value. Habiba Abderrahim, 2025. DOI 10.57967/hf/5189.

name: TounsiBench
description: The dedicated Tunisian LLM instruction benchmark. Ben Hassine, Arrak, Addhoum, Wilson, EMNLP 2025 (pp. 34627–34642).

name: How Well Do LLMs Understand Tunisian Arabic?
description: Parallel Tunizi ↔ standard Tunisian ↔ English corpus with sentiment labels; benchmarks LLMs on transliteration, translation, sentiment. arXiv, Nov 2025. **[open]** (arXiv).

name: linagora/TunisianMMLU
description: MMLU-style multiple-choice benchmark in Tunisian Derja: 22,027 questions (card figure) over 44 subjects, machine-translated from MMLU, ArabicMMLU and DarijaMMLU. LINAGORA, Feb 2025. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

name: LINAGORA / Labess training stack
description: linagora/Tunisian_Derja_Dataset — 2.23M-row Derja corpus used for continual pre-training (also listed under raw corpora). **[open]**.

name: Tunisia.AI / khaled123 (Khaled Bouzaiene)
description: khaled123/Tunisian_Dialectic_English_Derja (~1.66M rows, Derja↔English, translations + sentiment + generation), khaled123/tunisiansynthinstract (~266k synthetic instructions), khaled123/Tunisianderjasynthtranslation (~436k), khaled123/tuniset (~29k). 2024. **[open]**. (Note: this account hosts many datasets of uneven quality — some are noisy dumps; verify before use.)

name: Other
description: ESPRIT-Derja-Instruct — the 7,013-example Arabic/Arabizi instruction set behind ESPRIT-Derja-Qwen3-8B-v2 (3,494 GPT-4o-distilled pairs in both scripts + 25 manual). The model card says it "will be published separately"; **not released** as of 4 Sept 2026, so it carries no access tag.

name: TARIC — Tunisian Arabic Railway Interaction Corpus
description: ~20 hours of authentic railway-station dialogues at the Tunis station ticket offices (4,662 dialogues, 18,657 statements, 71,684 words per the paper), manually transcribed in Arabic script with diacritics, plus a rule-based phonetic (pronunciation) dictionary (grapheme-to-phoneme word error ≈ 9%). Masmoudi, Ellouze Khmekhem, Estève, Hadrich Belguith, Habash (MIRACL Sfax, LIUM Le Mans, CCLS Columbia), LREC 2014.

name: STAC — Spoken Tunisian Arabic Corpus
description: ~4.8 hours (4h50m31s per the paper) of spontaneous speech — ~3.5 h of TV/radio talk shows plus ~30 min of re-transcribed TuDiCoI railway dialogues — manually transcribed in two orthographic versions (OTTA and CODA-TUN) with morpho-syntactic and disfluency annotation. Zribi, Ellouze, Hadrich Belguith, Blache, Research in Computing Science 90, 2015 (open access). The authors describe it as the first Tunisian resource with several annotation types.

name: TunSwitch (TunSwitch-TO + TunSwitch-CS)
description: Code-switching speech (SpeechBrain format). Ben Abdallah, Kabboudi, Kanoun, Zaiem (Tunis Business School, Univ. of Michigan-Dearborn, Abshore, Télécom Paris), 2023/2024.

name: LinTO Audio & Textual Datasets for Tunisian Arabic
description: ~93 hours of audio (~81.6h labeled), 20,895 files / ~76k segments; aggregated from YouTube, podcasts, MASC, TunSwitch, OneStory, etc. Naouara, Lorré, Louradour (LINAGORA Labs), 2025. The largest openly-packaged Tunisian ASR training collection.

name: TARIC-SLU
description: Spoken language understanding extension of TARIC: ~8 hours, 2,043 dialogues / 17,816 utterances, railway dialogues annotated with 60 slot concepts. Mdhaffar, Bougares, de Mori, Zaiem, Ravanelli, Estève, LREC-COLING 2024. (The 108-speaker figure belongs to the original TARIC collection; the SLU splits list 5/39/38 speakers.)

name: SLURP-TN
description: Tunisian version of the SLURP SLU resource: ~5 hours, 4,165 sentences, 55 native speakers, 6 domains. Elleuch, Mdhaffar, Estève, Bougares (LIA Avignon + Elyadata), 2026.

name: TEDxTN
description: First publicly available Tunisian→English speech-translation corpus: 108 TEDx talks (~25 hours), code-switched Tunisian, speakers from 11+ regions; Tunisian transcript + English translation + annotation guidelines. Bougares, Mdhaffar, Elleuch, Estève, ArabicNLP 2025.

name: TuniFra
description: The first open Tunisian↔French code-switch speech-translation corpus: 15 hours of native Tunisian speech, orthographically transcribed and manually translated into French, for ASR and Tunisian→French speech translation. Choux, Avila, Crego, Bougares, Laurent (+ Riguidel on the PDF byline), ArabicNLP 2025.

name: TuDiCoI — Tunisian Dialect Corpus Interlocutor
description: Spoken railway-ticket dialogue corpus (Derja), transcribed; the original is about 8 hours / 6,533 utterances (per the STAC and TARIC-SLU papers). The arbml HF mirror holds only 434 rows, one column, no card or licence. One of the earliest Tunisian dialogue resources.

name: IWSLT 2022 Tunisian Conversational Speech (LDC2022E01 / LDC2025S05)
description: Large three-way (audio + transcript + English translation) conversational telephone speech corpus, 210 h of audio (LDC), of which 175 h carry transcripts and English translations (the IWSLT task used 160 h); orthographic transcripts in Buckwalter transliteration, IPA on a subset; 8 kHz; 1,188 conversations collected 2016–2017. Basis of the IWSLT dialectal speech-translation task.

name: TuniSpeech-21h
description: Multi-domain corpus: 21h 6m, 32,294 segments, 187 speakers (120 M / 67 F); social-media + broadcast (politics, sports, culture, cooking, etc.). Sghaier, Bellagha, Zrigui (Univ. of Monastir), ICAART 2026. Ships with a Wav2Vec2 vs Whisper benchmark (best: Whisper-large-v2, WER 24.74%).

name: OpenSLR SLR46 — Tunisian_MSA
description: 11.2 hours of read/prompted utterances by 118 Tunisian speakers — but the **content is Modern Standard Arabic**, not Derja. Useful for Tunisian-accent MSA acoustic modeling only.

name: CALL MY NET 2 (CMN2) / 2018 NIST SRE (LDC2020S04)
description: Tunisian Arabic conversational telephone speech (PSTN + VOIP, 8 kHz) collected by LDC in Tunisia via the Call My Net 2 protocol, plus English web-video audio from the VAST project. LDC gives **~396 hours for the release as a whole** — the Tunisian-only portion is not stated separately, so treat 396h as an upper bound, not a Tunisian figure.

name: Arbi-Houssem/Tunisian_dataset_STT-TTS15s_filtred1.0
description: 1,103 rows (1,032 train / 71 validation) of timestamped Derja transcripts with a `speaker` id; the LinTO aggregate repackages 1,029 of them as ~3h50m. No card, no licence tag. Usable for STT and TTS. 2024.

name: oddadmix/lahgtna-v3-small
description: Dialect-**balanced** multi-dialect Arabic ASR set: ~54.6k rows, 52k train / 2.6k test, 13 dialects including Tunisian, seed 42; columns `audio`, `transcript_text`, `language` (WER is scored on a normalised, undiacritised form of the text). Ahmed Wasfy (oddadmix), 2026.

name: FARUKxAUTO/tunisian-asr-cleaned
description: Tunisian ASR set, **46,034 train / 5,415 validation / 2,707 test** (54,156 rows), 16 kHz audio paired with a `sentence` transcript. ~15.7 GB. Uploaded 16 Mar 2026. On size alone this is one of the largest Tunisian ASR sets listed here, and it is essentially undiscovered (a few dozen downloads when checked).

name: oddadmix/arabic-audio-collection-tunisian-deep-confessions
description: **37,156** transcribed chunks (~175 hours per the card), ~20.0 GB, 16 kHz, segmented from the *Deep Confessions* podcast (Tunisian; the card names the show, not the platform). Fields: `chunk_id`, `audio`, `transcript_text`, `duration`, `original_video_id`. Ahmed Wasfy (oddadmix), 2026.

name: Fares11/senior_tunisian_voice
description: **5,377** rows, ~2.39 GB. Fields: `audio_id`, `audio`, `transcript`, plus a nested `segments` list carrying `start`/`end` and **both** `transcript` and `transcript_raw` per segment. Apache-2.0, 2026.

name: Undocumented community audio sets
description: safara/TunisianOnly — an `audio_files/` directory of `.wav` clips (~92 MB total; file count not verified) with `train.csv` / `dev.csv` / `test.csv` carrying `filename`, `transcription` and `duration` columns, i.e. **transcripts exist**, but the header casing differs between splits, which breaks the HF viewer. ⚠️ No dataset card and no licence, May 2025. Recorded here flagged rather than omitted. **[open]** (access only; no licence).

name: TunArTTS — Tunisian Arabic Text-To-Speech Corpus
description: First Tunisian TTS resource: 3+ hours, single male speaker, 44.1 kHz, manually diacritized. Laouirine, Kammoun, Bougares, LREC-COLING 2024. Tacotron2 + FastSpeech2 baselines (best MOS 3.88 via transfer from LJSpeech).

name: Habibi — Unified-Dialectal Arabic Speech Synthesis
description: Multi-dialect Arabic TTS framework + benchmark (12+ dialects, zero-shot voice cloning). Code: SWivid/Habibi-TTS. Tunisian (`TUN`) is a supported inference dialect but **not** one of the 7 benchmark subsets (MSA, SAU, UAE, ALG, IRQ, EGY, MAR). Code MIT; released models CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. **[open]** (Tunisian supported, not benchmarked).

name: Community and commercial Tunisian TTS
description: SpeechGen Tunisian TTS (ar-TN) — commercial text-to-speech with Tunisian voices (e.g., Hedi, Reem). Not open/research; noted for completeness. **[commercial]**.

name: ADI-20 — Arabic Dialect Identification dataset
description: 3,556 hours across 19 dialects + MSA; expands ADI-17 and explicitly **adds Tunisian**. Elleuch et al., Interspeech 2025. The first large spoken-ADI set to include Tunisian.

name: Text and Speech-based Tunisian Sub-Dialects Identification (LREC 2020)
description: Distinguishes Tunisian sub-dialects (Tunis / Sfax / Sousse / Tataouine) from text and speech; the spoken corpus (1,673 utterances) is described as freely distributed. Ben Abdallah, Kchaou, Bougares. **[open]** (paper).

name: NADI 2025 — First Multidialectal Arabic Speech Processing Shared Task
description: Subtask 1: spoken dialect ID over eight dialects (Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Mauritania, Morocco, Palestine, UAE, Yemen — **Tunisian not included**; the winning team pre-trained on ADI-20); Subtask 2: multidialectal ASR; Subtask 3: diacritic restoration. Talafha et al., 2025.

name: NADI 2026 — Multidialectal Arabic Speech Processing
description: Speech-focused, and strongly Tunisian-relevant. Tasks include country-level / mixed / **code-switched ASR** (subtask 1.3 is Tunisian⇄English⇄French code-switching), spoken dialect ID, dialectal TTS, spoken language translation (8 dialects→English, none Tunisian), and SLU (intent + slot filling).

name: SLURP-TN baselines
description: Baseline SpeechBrain recipes for the SLURP-TN dataset. Elyadata. **[open]** (GitHub).

name: IWSLT 2022 / 2023 dialectal speech translation
description: Tunisian→English speech translation task (the 2023 edition ran under the low-resource track). Data prep/scoring: kevinduh/iwslt22-dialect. **[open]** (scripts); the underlying audio is the LDC Tunisian conversational corpus listed above, which is **[paywalled]**.

name: Labess-7b-chat
description: Instruction-tuned Tunisian Derja chat model. Wajdi Ghezaiel and Jean-Pierre Lorré (LINAGORA), 2025. 7B, Apache-2.0.

name: ESPRIT-Derja-Qwen3-8B-v2
description: Tunisian instruct model. ESPRIT School of Engineering (Mourad Zerai), 2026. Qwen3-8B + LoRA (rank 32) on 7,013 Arabic/Arabizi Tunisian instruction examples (ESPRIT-Derja-Instruct: 3,494 GPT-4o-distilled pairs in both scripts + 25 manual; not yet released separately). The first Tunisian instruct model that explicitly handles Arabizi (3=ع, 7=ح, 9=ق…). Apache-2.0.

name: TunBERT
description: The canonical Tunisian BERT. iCompass + InstaDeep, 2021. BERT-base architecture (12 layers, 768 hidden; the HF conversion has 110M params), pretrained on ~500k Tunisian social-media comments (~67 MB Common-Crawl-based).

name: tunis-ai/TunBERT
description: HF-hosted, ready-to-use conversion of TunBERT (NeMo → safetensors) wired for `transformers` text classification (tagged `dataset:tsac`; the card reports no fine-tuning numbers). The most-downloaded TunBERT on the Hub. ~0.1B params, MIT. **[open]**.

name: ziedsb19/tunbert_zied
description: Independent Tunisian RoBERTa-style masked LM. Zied Sbabti, 2021. Trained on ~600,000 Tunisian phrases; handles Arabizi (use `BertTokenizer`, not `AutoTokenizer`). **[open]**.

name: hamzabouajila/distilled_tunbert
description: Distilled TunBERT (DistilBERT student, ~66M params, ~1.83× faster). Hamza Bouajila, 2025. Teacher = tunis-ai/TunBERT; trained on the open tunisian-derja-unified-raw-corpus. Good for classification, not embeddings (card is honest about this). MIT. **[open]**.

name: SalahZa/Tunisian_Automatic_Speech_Recognition
description: SpeechBrain semi-supervised WavLM-large + CTC. Ben Abdallah, Kabboudi, Kanoun, Zaiem, 2023 (no licence tag on the repo). WER/CER: TARIC 10.55/6.22, IWSLT 39.53/21.18, TunSwitch-TO 25.54/9.67. Demo. Paper arXiv:2309.11327. **[open]**.

name: SalahZa/Code_Switched_Tunisian_Speech_Recognition
description: Code-switched ASR (wav2vec2 TN/FR/EN, SpeechBrain). WER/CER: TunSwitch-CS 29.47/12.44. Demo (Space in runtime error when checked, Sept 2026). Apache-2.0. **[open]**.

name: linagora/linto-asr-ar-tn-0.1
description: Kaldi TDNN / Vosk + SRILM LM. LINAGORA, uploaded Sept 2024 (paper 2025). WER/CER: TARIC 16.06/10.60, TunSwitch-CS 20.51/17.72, TunSwitch-TO 22.54/11.13. Android/Raspberry-Pi variant. Training code: linagora-labs/ASR_train_kaldi_tunisian. Apache-2.0. **[open]**.

name: TuniSpeech-AI/whisper-tunisian-dialect
description: Whisper-large-v2 fine-tuned (LoRA merged; 1.54B params). Sghaier, Bellagha, Zrigui, 2026. WER 24.74 / CER 8.32 on TuniSpeech-21h — the figures are on the dataset card, not the model card. Demo. cc-by-nc-4.0. **[open]** (weights).

name: oddadmix/whisper-large-v3-arabic-dialectal-v2
description: Whisper-large-v3 (1.54B) fine-tuned for **13 Arabic dialects**, Tunisian among them. Ahmed Wasfy (oddadmix), 2026. Trained on `oddadmix/lahgtna-v3-small` (52k train / 2.6k test, dialect-balanced).

name: oddadmix/Whisperv3-tunisian-codeswitch
description: Whisper-large-v3 **full** fine-tune (1.54B params) for Tunisian ↔ French/English **code-switched** ASR, built for **NADI 2026 subtask 1.3**. Ahmed Wasfy (oddadmix), uploaded 28 Jul 2026.

name: medfadiabaidi/whisper-small-tunisian-asr
description: `openai/whisper-small` (244M) fine-tuned on TEDxTN. Declared in the card's `model-index`: **WER 37.99 / CER 18.77** on the TEDxTN test split. 2025.

name: Classic ASR systems (papers)
description: ASR system for Tunisian dialect (Kaldi, TARIC), LRE 2018 — Masmoudi, Bougares, Ellouze, Estève, Belguith; LRE 52, pp. 249–267. WER 22.6% (abstract). **[paywalled]** (preprint on ResearchGate).

name: KBayoud/qwen3-asr-tunisian-telephony-augmented
description: Qwen3-ASR (`Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration`) fine-tune, uploaded 4 Aug 2026 (KBayoud). **No model card at all** — "Tunisian telephony, augmented" is the repo name, nothing more is documented. **[gated]** (manual approval required for the weights).

name: Community Whisper fine-tunes for Tunisian (Jul–Aug 2026, grouped)
description: Small community ASR releases, grouped in one entry: awaxsama/whisper-small-tunisian-arabic and whisper-tiny-tunisian-arabic (Aug 2026, Apache-2.0, trained on linagora/linto-dataset-audio-ar-tn-augmented) · maxvu0/whisper-large-v2-tunisian-lora (17 Aug 2026, LoRA adapter; licence "[More Information Needed]").

name: oddadmix/lahgtna-omnivoice-v2 (لهجتنا)
description: Multi-dialect Arabic TTS built on OmniVoice (Qwen3-0.6B backbone; 0.6B params), aiming at a single unified model across Arabic dialects. Ahmed Wasfy (oddadmix), 2026. **Tunisia is ticked on the dialect roadmap**, alongside Egypt, Saudi, Morocco, Iraq, Sudan, Palestine, Lebanon, Syria, Libya, Bahrain, Yemen, Algeria.

name: Ghazouaniwala/silma-tts-derja
description: F5-TTS Tunisian Derja fine-tunes of silma-ai/silma-tts, trained on the LinTO Tunisian audio dataset. Apache-2.0. Five repos uploaded Jul 2026: `silma-tts-derja`, `-v2`, `-v2-1`, `-v3a`, `-v4a`.

name: Mui17/tunisian-xtts-v1
description: XTTS-based Tunisian TTS, uploaded 14 Aug 2026, Apache-2.0 (Mui17). Community release; no published evaluation. **[open]**.

name: oddadmix/dialect-router-v0.2
description: Arabic dialect identification: text classification into **15 labels — 13 Arabic dialects, MSA, and English**. Tunisian is label `tn`. Ahmed Wasfy (oddadmix), 2026. Fine-tune of `asafaya/bert-mini-arabic`; **11.6M parameters**, 512-token input. Built as the routing backbone of the Lahgtna TTS pipeline, but usable standalone.

name: Ghazouaniwala/trocr-tunisian-arabic
description: TrOCR fine-tune for Tunisian Arabic text recognition, uploaded 2 Aug 2026 (Ghazouaniwala). The registry's first OCR entry; the repo has no model card and no licence tag (checked 4 Sept 2026). **[open]**.
